questions.question: Which of these is an organisation that promotes sustainable management and conservation of tropical forests?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Tropical Timber Organization.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• International Tropical Timber Organization is an organization that promotes sustainable management and conservation of tropical forests.
 
• International Tropical Timber Organization was formed in 1986.
 
• Its headquarters is located at **Yokohama in Japan.**
 
• Its members represent about 80% of the world’s tropical forests and 90% of the global tropical timber trade.
 
• The most recent **international tropical timber agreement 2006** entered into force on 7th December 2011.
 
• The main objectives of the International Tropical Timber Organization are:
 
 
• Develops internationally agreed with policy guidelines and norms to encourage sustainable forest management (SFM) and sustainable tropical timber industries and trade.
 
• Assists tropical member countries through projects and other activities.
 
• Collects analyze and disseminates data on the production and trade of tropical timber.
 
• Promotes sustainable tropical timber supply chains.
 
• Helps develop capacity in tropical forestry.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **United Nations Forum on Forests **is a subsidiary body of the Economic and Social Council of the United Nations (ECOSOC) with the main objective to promote the management, conservation, and sustainable development of all types of forests.
 
• **Greenpeace** is a non-governmental environmental organization founded in 1971.
 
• **World Wide Fund for Nature** is a science-based organization that addresses issues such as the conservation of species and its habitats, climate change, water, and environmental education, among many others.

questions.question: Bananas turn brown in colour because:

options.text: an enzyme converts starch into sugar
the air reacts with the enzymes in the banana
Bisphosphonates reacts with the enzymes in the banana
an enzyme converts sugar into starch

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**the air reacts with the enzymes in the banana**__.

 
• Bananas turn brown in color because the **air reacts with the enzymes in the banana**.
 
• The life cycle of a banana starts with a deep **green color**.
 
• The deep green color of bananas changes to a **delicious yellow** and ends with a brown color.
 
• The unripened bananas are a light green color that begins to **yellow as they ripen**.
 
• Bananas contain an enzyme called **polyphenol oxidase** that reacts with oxygen in the atmosphere and coats the banana with a sort of rust that accounts for the dark brown color.
 
• **Ethylene** hormone helps for the ripening process.
 
• Large amounts of ethylene leads to the decaying of yellow pigments in bananas and it will change into brown color.
 
• The processes of formation of brown spots on a banana is called **enzymatic browning**.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a term associated with credit?
questions.solution:
__**Stamp by the finance minister**__ is NOT correct.

 
• Credit refers to an agreement in which the lender supplies the borrower with money, goods, or services in return for the promise of future payment.
 
• The terms associated with credit are:
 
 
• Interest rate.
 
• Collateral.
 
• Necessary documents.
 
 
 
• Every loan(credit) agreement specifies an** interest rate** which the borrower must pay to the lender along with the repayment of the principal.
 
• Lenders may demand **collateral (security)** against loans.
 
 
• Collateral is an asset that the borrower owns such as land, vehicle, building, or deposits with banks, and uses this as a guarantee to a lender until the loan is repaid.
 
• The lender has the right to sell the asset or collateral to obtain payment If the borrower fails to repay the loan.
 
 
 
• One had to submit necessary valid **documents **to the bank for the approval of loans.

questions.question: On which of the below can an excise duty charged?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Goods manufactured.**__

 
• **Excise duty** is a tax imposed on goods for their production, licensing, and sale.
 
• Excise duty is an **indirect tax.**
 
• Central excise duty is a tax that is charged on such excisable goods that are manufactured in India and are meant for domestic consumption.
 
• It is mandatory to pay Central Excise duty payable on the goods manufactured unless exempted.
 
• Excise duty is the opposite of **Customs duty.**
 
• The Goods and Services Tax (GST) subsumed many types of excise duty.
 
• At present, excise duty applies only to **petroleum and liquor.**
 
• The union excise duties form the most significant part of the central taxes.

questions.question: What was the amendment done to the Indian Constitution by 52ⁿd amendment done in 1985?

options.text: Amendment to the Union and State lists with respect to raising of taxes
The words ‘socialist secular’ added to the preamble
Formation of Sikkim as a state within the Indian Union

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Anti-defection law was included.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__** 

__
 
• **Anti-defection law** was included in the Indian Constitution by the 52ⁿd amendment.
 
• The 52ⁿd amendment was passed in the year **1985.**
 
• It also added the** tenth schedule** to the Indian constitution.
 
• The tenth schedule deals with the disqualification of members of Parliament and State legislature on the ground of defection.
 
• The Anti-defection law was passed by Lok Sabha on **30th January 1985.**
 
• Anti-defection law was by Rajya Sabha on **31st January 1985.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• **The sixth amendment **of the Indian constitution amended the Union List and State List with respect to raising taxes.
 
• **The 42ⁿd amendment** added the words ‘socialist secular’ added to the preamble.
 
• **The 36th amendment** deals with the formation of Sikkim as a state within the Indian Union.

questions.question: Which articles of the Indian Constitution cover the fundamental right against exploitation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Articles 23-24.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points:__**

__
 
• **Articles 23-24** of the Indian Constitution cover the fundamental right against exploitation.
 
• **Articles 23** prohibits human beings and other similar forms of forced labour.
 
 
• Nothing in article 23 shall prevent the State from imposing compulsory service for public purpose, and in imposing such service the State shall not make any discrimination on grounds only of religion, race, caste or class or any of them.
 
 
 
• **Articles 24** prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in any factory, mine, or other hazardous activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Articles 14** says that all persons are equal before the law and entitled to equal protection of the laws.
 
• **Articles 18** abolishes titles except military and academic.
 
• **Articles 19** guarantees six fundamental freedoms to all citizens.
 
• **Articles 22** provides protection against arbitrary arrest and detention.
 
• **Articles 29** provides the protection of the interests of minorities.
 
• **Articles 30** provides the right of minorities to establish and administer the educational institutes.

questions.question:
Arrange the following events in correct chronology:

1) Champaran Satyagraha against indigo plantation
2) Starting of non-cooperation Khilafat movement
3) Rowlatt Satyagraha
4) Arrival of Simon commission in India
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1-3-2-4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Champaran Satyagraha** against indigo plantation was in 1917.

 
 
• Champaran Satyagraha was **Mahathma Gandhi's first satyagraha in India.**
 
• It took place at Champaran in Bihar.
 
• Demand for high rent and illegal dues by European planters leads to Champaran Satyagraha.
 
• British agreed to the demands of the farmers at the end of this satyagraha.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Satyagraha** was in 1919.
 
 
• It was against the anarchical and revolutionary crimes act(Rowlett act) passed by the British.
 
• The Rowlett act was passed on** 6th February 1919.**
 
• Gandhiji called this act as "**black act'**".
 
• The act empowered the British government to arrest any person without reason, search any place without warrant and imprison anyone without trial.
 
 
 
• **The Non-cooperation Khilafat movement** was started in 1920.
 
 
• The non-cooperation movement is the **first mass political movement under Gandhiji in India.**
 
• The attainment of swaraj by peaceful means was the main goal of this movement.
 
• The non-cooperation movement was called off by Gandhiji due to the Chauri Chaura incident.
 
 
 
• The** Simon commission** arrived in India in 1928.
 
 
• It was formed to study constitutional reforms and make recommendations to the government in India.
 
• Simon commission was an all-white commission without any Indian members.
 
• It was formed on **26th November 1927.**
 
• Simon commission arrived in India on **3rd February 1928.**
 
• Simon commission submitted its reports on 27th May 1930.

questions.question: Which of the motions is passed in the parliament to remove the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Impeachment Motion**__.

 
• An impeachment motion is passed in the parliament to remove the** President of India.**
 
• The impeachment is a **quasi-judicial procedure.**
 
• **Article 61** of the Indian constitution deals with the processes of impeachment of the president.
 
• The only ground for the impeachment of the president is "**violation of the constitution**".
 
• The impeachment procedure can be initiated by either house of the parliament.
 
• The charges are contained in a notice that should be signed by **one-fourth** of the total members of the initiating house.
 
• A **14 days advance notice** should be given to the president after initiating the procedure.
 
• The president can defend himself by taking the service of the attorney general of India or any other law officer of his choice.
 
• The impeachment procedure requires a special majority.
 
• If the other house also passes a resolution by **2/3 majority** of the total members of the house, then the president will be removed from his office from the date on which the bill is so passed.
 
• **No president **has so far impeached in India.
